From 2195574dc6d9017d32ac346987e12659f931d932 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Xiang Mei <xmei5@asu.edu>
Date: Tue, 14 Apr 2026 15:14:01 -0700
Subject: [PATCH] netfilter: nfnetlink_osf: fix divide-by-zero in
 OSF_WSS_MODULO

nf_osf_match_one() computes ctx->window % f->wss.val in the
OSF_WSS_MODULO branch with no guard for f->wss.val == 0. A
CAP_NET_ADMIN user can add such a fingerprint via nfnetlink; a
subsequent matching TCP SYN divides by zero and panics the kernel.

Reject the bogus fingerprint in nfnl_osf_add_callback() above the
per-option for-loop. f->wss is per-fingerprint, not per-option, so
the check must run regardless of f->opt_num (including 0). Also
reject wss.wc >= OSF_WSS_MAX; nf_osf_match_one() already treats that
as "should not happen".

Crash:
 Oops: divide error: 0000 [#1] SMP KASAN NOPTI
 RIP: 0010:nf_osf_match_one (net/netfilter/nfnetlink_osf.c:98)
 Call Trace:
 <IRQ>
  nf_osf_match (net/netfilter/nfnetlink_osf.c:220)
  xt_osf_match_packet (net/netfilter/xt_osf.c:32)
  ipt_do_table (net/ipv4/netfilter/ip_tables.c:348)
  nf_hook_slow (net/netfilter/core.c:622)
  ip_local_deliver (net/ipv4/ip_input.c:265)
  ip_rcv (include/linux/skbuff.h:1162)
  __netif_receive_skb_one_core (net/core/dev.c:6181)
  process_backlog (net/core/dev.c:6642)
  __napi_poll (net/core/dev.c:7710)
  net_rx_action (net/core/dev.c:7945)
  handle_softirqs (kernel/softirq.c:622)

Fixes: 11eeef41d5f6 ("netfilter: passive OS fingerprint xtables match")
Reported-by: Weiming Shi <bestswngs@gmail.com>
Suggested-by: Florian Westphal <fw@strlen.de>
Suggested-by: Pablo Neira Ayuso <pablo@netfilter.org>
Signed-off-by: Xiang Mei <xmei5@asu.edu>
Reviewed-by: Fernando Fernandez Mancera <fmancera@suse.de>
Signed-off-by: Pablo Neira Ayuso <pablo@netfilter.org>

diff --git a/net/netfilter/nfnetlink_osf.c b/net/netfilter/nfnetlink_osf.c
index d64ce21c7b55..9de91fdd107c 100644
--- a/net/netfilter/nfnetlink_osf.c
+++ b/net/netfilter/nfnetlink_osf.c
@@ -320,6 +320,10 @@ static int nfnl_osf_add_callback(struct sk_buff *skb,
 	if (f->opt_num > ARRAY_SIZE(f->opt))
 		return -EINVAL;
 
+	if (f->wss.wc >= OSF_WSS_MAX ||
+	    (f->wss.wc == OSF_WSS_MODULO && f->wss.val == 0))
+		return -EINVAL;
+
 	for (i = 0; i < f->opt_num; i++) {
 		if (!f->opt[i].length || f->opt[i].length > MAX_IPOPTLEN)
 			return -EINVAL;
-- 
2.34.1

The patch modifies `net/netfilter/nfnetlink_osf.c` to add input validation in the `nfnl_osf_add_callback()` function. It inserts a check before the per-option for-loop that rejects a fingerprint if:

1. The window size code `f->wss.wc` is greater than or equal to `OSF_WSS_MAX` (i.e., out of valid range).
2. The window size code is `OSF_WSS_MODULO` and `f->wss.val` is zero (which would cause a division by zero in `nf_osf_match_one()`).

This prevents users with `CAP_NET_ADMIN` from adding a bogus fingerprint that would trigger a kernel panic (divide-by-zero) when matching a TCP SYN packet against it. The relationship between the two parts is that the validation at the add callback eliminates the risk at the match point, fixing the security bug.

You are a programming expert.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
In `nf_osf_match_one`:
```c
if (f->wss.wc == OSF_WSS_MODULO)
    delta = ctx->window % f->wss.val;
```
In `nfnl_osf_add_callback`:
```c
f = nla_data(osf_attrs[OSF_ATTR_FINGER]);
/* No validation of f->wss.wc or f->wss.val follows */
```
Reason:
The division `ctx->window % f->wss.val` causes a divide-by-zero crash when `f->wss.val` is 0. A privileged user can supply such a fingerprint via nfnetlink because `nfnl_osf_add_callback` accepts the user data without checking the window size fields. The missing validation allows a zero divisor to be stored, leading to the panic when a matching TCP SYN packet triggers the OSF match.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
In `nfnl_osf_add_callback`, after validating `f->opt_num`:
```c
if (f->wss.wc >= OSF_WSS_MAX ||
    (f->wss.wc == OSF_WSS_MODULO && f->wss.val == 0))
    return -EINVAL;
```
Reason:
This check rejects two invalid fingerprint conditions before the fingerprint is stored:
- `f->wss.wc >= OSF_WSS_MAX` is a guard against out-of-bounds window class values, which are already treated as “should not happen” in the match function.
- `f->wss.wc == OSF_WSS_MODULO && f->wss.val == 0` directly prevents the division-by-zero by requiring a non‑zero modulus value.
By failing early in the add callback, the kernel never stores the malformed fingerprint, so the division in `nf_osf_match_one` is never executed with a zero divisor.
